record.paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
record.original_question: Can PRUW be generalized from the existing single-client system model to a multi-client system model in which private read-write communication is defined for a group of clients, the same privacy, security, and correctness requirements are maintained, and communication cost is reduced by combining queries, answers, or updates from multiple clients?

evidence.quote: Private read-update-write (PRUW) [26]–[29] is the concept where a user downloads, updates and uploads the updates back to a chosen section of a data storage system, without revealing the content downloaded, uploaded or their positions, e.g., updated section index. PRUW is essentially the combination of private reading and private writing described previously.

All existing work on PRUW [26]–[28], [47], [48], [51], [52] consider a single client in the system model as shown in Fig. 9, i.e., all client-server communications are defined for a single client. A multi-client PRUW system model, where the private read-write process is defined from the perspective of a group of clients as opposed to defining it on an individual client with the same privacy, security and correctness requirements could be a promising future direction as it may result in a reduced communication cost, from combining queries/answers/updates of multiple clients.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a distributed storage system in which a database is replicated (or coded) across $N$ non-colluding servers. Each server stores a model partitioned into $M$ disjoint sections (submodels). A single-client Private Read-Update-Write (PRUW) protocol allows a client to (i) privately download the contents of a chosen section $\theta \in \{1,\dots,M\}$, (ii) compute an update locally, and (iii) upload the update back to the same section, subject to the following requirements:
- Privacy: no server (or any allowed colluding subset) learns the index $\theta$ of the section read or written.
- Security: no server learns the values downloaded or the values of the update uploaded.
- Correctness: after the protocol, the chosen section is correctly updated at all servers, and the client correctly recovers the requested section's contents.

The communication cost is measured as the total number of symbols exchanged between the client(s) and the servers per unit of information read/written.

Problem. Generalize the PRUW model to a multi-client setting in which $K \geq 2$ clients simultaneously interact with the $N$ servers. Concretely, design a protocol satisfying:
1. Each client $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ privately reads from a chosen section $\theta_k$ and privately writes an update to that section, with the same privacy, security, and correctness guarantees as in the single-client PRUW model (extended to apply jointly to the group of clients, so that the multi-set $\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_K\}$ and all update/read values remain hidden from any non-colluding subset of servers).
2. The protocol combines (aggregates or jointly encodes) queries, answers, and/or updates across the $K$ clients so as to achieve a strictly smaller total communication cost (per client, or in aggregate) than $K$ independent executions of the best known single-client PRUW protocol.

Determine whether such a multi-client PRUW protocol exists, and characterize the optimal achievable read and write communication costs as functions of $N$, $M$, and $K$ (and any colluding parameters).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search shows that existing PRUW work (including PRUW in federated submodel learning, with sparsification, and with heterogeneous databases) is formulated for a single client interacting with the servers. No publication was located that formalizes a multi-client PRUW system model with combined queries/answers/updates and characterizes its communication cost. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Private Read Update Write (PRUW) in Federated Submodel Learning (FSL): Communication Efficient Schemes With and Without Sparsification
status_evidence.snippet: PRUW is the process of privately performing FSL by reading from and writing to the required submodel without revealing the submodel index or the values of updates.
status_evidence.claim: Existing PRUW formulations are stated for a single client reading/writing the chosen submodel.

status_evidence.title: Private Read Update Write (PRUW) With Heterogeneous Databases
status_evidence.snippet: PRUW with heterogeneous databases studied as a single-client read/update/write problem.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up PRUW variants continue to consider the single-client system model.

status_evidence.title: Rate Distortion Tradeoff in Private Read Update Write in Federated Submodel Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the rate-distortion tradeoff in PRUW under the standard single-client model.
status_evidence.claim: No multi-client PRUW model with combined communication has been formalized in the located literature.
